title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and hygiene
author: Priya Rao
description: This PR consolidates several CI workflows (lint, unit-test, integration-test, and release automation) into a unified set of GitHub Actions workflows to improve cache efficiency, reduce duplicated steps across repos, and standardize job names/outputs for observability. Motivation: we recently saw CI time regressions and cache misses across the monorepo; unifying workflows reduces matrix size and improves parallel cache hits. Key changes include: - Split lint/test/release into reusable workflow templates under .github/workflows/templates. - Consolidated NodeJS build matrix to use node:20, pinned action versions, and introduced a shared build cache step. - Standardized job names and annotations so dashboards and alerting rules map consistently. - Added a lightweight verification job for release automation that runs only on release/* branches. - Introduced a reusable 'job-setup' composite action for common steps (checkout, cache restore, setup-node, install). - Fixed flaky lint rule ordering and updated eslint/prettier configs to align with repo rules. - Removed several legacy CI files and deprecated Azure pipeline stubs. Checklist: - [x] Implement reusable templates - [x] Update affected repositories to call new workflows - [x] Update release automation and release-drafter config - [x] Smoke test in redwood and redwood-docs - [x] Documentation updated (CONTRIBUTING.md) Rollout: staged rollouts were run across 'redwood' core first, then SDKs and docs. Notable follow-ups: final tuning of cache key for pnpm lockfile, and a small fix to an integration test timeout that flaked during reruns. Breaking changes: None expected - most jobs are opt-in by repo via workflow_dispatch or by matching branches. Related: ENG-2145 describes CI cost and flakiness metrics prompting this work. See the Linear ticket for benchmarking numbers.
